findings.title: Compliance percentage mismatch (Results, paragraph 1 (EMA compliance))
findings.description: TOOL ACTUALLY CALLED: check_count_percent (the `technique` enum has no entry for it; grim_percentage is the nearest registered percentage-check family, and check_count_percent is the strictly stronger version of it where the count is printed). The two counts are mutually consistent and independently verifiable: 6 surveys/day x 7 days x 107 participants = 4494, so the denominator is right. 3131/4494 = 69.67%, which the paper prints as 70.00% - rounded to a whole number but then formatted to two decimals, asserting a precision it does not have. Printing '69.67%' or '70%' would both have been accurate. Presentational defect, not a data-integrity one; nothing inferential depends on it.

findings.title: Multiplicity within person mediation
findings.description: Twelve mediation tests on the same 107 participants, testing one hypothesis across six correlated outcomes, with no correction stated anywhere. Uncorrected testing is ordinary practice, not misconduct - but the arithmetic is that the family-wise error rate reaches 46% and about 0.6 false positives are expected by chance. Three of the four uncorrected claims are robust (all p = .001, surviving even Bonferroni); the fourth, difficulties resisting eating at p = .026, exceeds every threshold (Bonferroni .0042, BH .0125, BY .0040). Surviving-claims interval is 3 to 3 - all four methods agree. The six LOC outcomes are measured on the same subjects and are plainly correlated, so Benjamini-Yekutieli

findings.title: Multiplicity between person mediation
findings.description: Weaker than the within-person family. Exactly one of twelve between-person mediation tests reached p < .05, and 0.6 false positives are expected by chance across a family of this size - so a single hit at p = .017 is close to what chance alone would deliver. Zero claims survive under all four correction methods. The paper states this between-person result in the Results and returns to it in the Discussion without noting that it is one significant test among twelve.

findings.title: Absence of evidence model3 null
findings.description: This is the paper's key dimensional-variation claim and the weakest of its null results. The 95% interval derived from the printed b and SE runs to 0.099, LARGER than the mediation effects reported as significant for general LOC eating (b = 0.10), driven/compelled to eat (b = 0.09) and felt disconnected (b = 0.09). The data therefore do not distinguish this dimension from those; the paper is contrasting significant with non-significant rather than testing the difference between them. No SESOI is stated, so equivalence cannot be assessed and no 'no effect' conclusion is licensed. findings.title: Table2 no duplication (Table 2, Models 1-6 direct-effect coefficients)
findings.description: Zero improbable overlaps. All 15 repeat groups carry `same_sample_caveat: true` - they are the affect -> emotion dysregulation paths, the same submodel estimated on the same 107 participants in every model, which SHOULD recur. Positive evidence AGAINST copy-paste: the between-person NA -> emotion dysregulation coefficient is 0.96 in Models 1-3 and 0.95 in Models 4-6, and the within-person PA -> emotion dysregulation p-value varies .038/.039/.040/.040/.042/.038 across models. That small, patternless variation is the signature of six genuinely separate re-estimations, which a duplicated block would not show.

findings.title: Nct identifier malformed (Participants and Procedures, second paragraph, first sentence)
findings.description: ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers are 'NCT' followed by exactly eight digits; the printed 'NCT0204349' has seven and does not resolve. The same malformed string appears in BOTH the XML and the PDF, so it is the paper's, not an extraction artifact. This is a typo in a load-bearing sentence - the registration is a reader's only route to the parent trial's protocol - which is why it is recorded rather than passed over. No claim is made about which digit is missing or what the correct identifier is; establishing that requires a registry lookup, outside this sweep. Recorded as `manual` because no forensic tool covers identifier format, and capped at `suspicious` accordingly.

findings.title: Near collinear construct overlap (Study Purpose, final paragraph)
findings.description: Not an arithmetic anomaly - r = .948 is well within bounds and no tool flags it. Recorded because the paper cites it in passing as evidence of 'overlap' when it in fact indicates the two constructs are barely distinguishable in this sample. The prior publication on this same dataset (Wonderlich et al. 2024) tested negative urgency as the mediator of the negative-affect-to-binge-eating path; the present paper tests emotion dysregulation. At this correlation those are close to the same analysis on the same participants, which is relevant to how independent the two sets of findings should be treated as being. No shared-variance figure is computed here, as that would be unaided arithmetic. Flagg

findings.title: Citation year discrepancy pdf vs xml
findings.description: The PDF is the PMC author manuscript and the XML the publisher version, so these are different versions of the same text and a copy-editing correction between them is the ordinary explanation. The XML uses 'Stefano et al. [2016]' consistently, including elsewhere on the same page; the PDF's single '2014' at this location appears to be the pre-correction reading. Recorded only so a reader working from the PDF is not confused. No accusation is implied.
